introduction: Hawaiʻi DHS accepts SNAP applications through PAIS or a signed paper application. Keep the tracking receipt and expect DHS to contact you for an interview.
description: Hawaiʻi DHS accepts SNAP applications through PAIS or a signed paper application. Keep the tracking receipt and expect DHS to contact you for an interview.

sections.who: DHS assesses household financial circumstances and other SNAP requirements. Its current page distinguishes broad-based categorical eligibility, households receiving certain cash benefits, and other income tests; do not use one income figure as a universal rule.
sections.get: Approved households receive SNAP food benefits through the Hawaiʻi EBT system. The decision explains the award and the household’s reporting and review responsibilities.
sections.docs:
• Prepare household members’ information and current income records.
  • Have relevant housing, childcare and other expense information available.
  • Use DHS’s case-specific request to identify required verification.
sections.apply:
1. Submit online or on paper

    Start from the DHS SNAP application page. It links PAIS and the paper form.

  2. Save the tracking receipt

    For online applications, DHS provides a receipt and tracking number. Paper forms must be signed and may be mailed or dropped off at a processing center.

  3. Complete the interview

    DHS contacts you for an interview. Provide requested verification and read the eligibility decision.
sections.after: Follow the reporting and recertification instructions in your notice. If PAIS is unavailable, use the paper route or call 1-855-643-1643 about assistance.
sections.sources: Checked October 1, 2026 using Hawaiʻi DHS SNAP eligibility and intake instructions. USA Assistance background guide. Program staff determine eligibility and available assistance.

faqs: Yes. DHS lists signed paper applications submitted by mail or drop-off.
Does a tracking number mean approval?
No. It confirms receipt; DHS still reviews eligibility and interviews the household.
Are all households tested against the same income rule?
No. The agency lists different eligibility categories. Let DHS assess the applicable one.

provenance.scope: Published eligibility, service purpose and application pathway; no unverified financial limits or deadlines included.
